findings.reason: the node must either extend `_population_has_live_work` to take the observed sessions (a change to a function the plan says needs none) or the plan must state that extension as part of §4, otherwise the second done-when bullet is unimplementable as written.
findings.text: §4 says "'No live run' is the answer of `_population_has_live_work(project, session=...)` … which already owns that judgement; it is not derived a second time", and says "the population it settles on is its own session plus the sessions it observes, not the whole project", but `_population_has_live_work` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:567) skips every pointer whose `owner` differs from the single `session` argument and never receives the follower's `observe_sessions`, so with `session=S` an observed peer session P whose run is still live is invisible; the mechanism as stated therefore cannot produce done-when bullet 2 ("A follower that observes a peer session whose run is still live does not settle") and a node trusting "already owns that judgement" would settle the follower while an observed run is live

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/session_host.py` (`SessionHost.handle`:350, `tick`:431), `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py` (`_population_has_live_work`:567), the `crew follow --lifetime` final-line path (`_follower_end_line`:651), `--observe-session` (:2184) and decision `pane-end` (line 131) all resolve; the new test file is a deliverable, not an anchor.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §4 names a negative control ("restarts a settled child immediately as today's backoff does") that fails the first case (a re-spawned idle child would print the idle line twice, breaking "delivered once"), and the four bullets are measurable against a temporary host-state fixture.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative control is "logged under the run directory" (a durable path under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>`), and the test's own "temporary host state directory" is a fixture, not the evidence store.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach §4's symbols or prose; the only identifiers are real code names (`SessionHost.handle`, `_population_has_live_work`) and the plan's own decision key `pane-end`.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4 asserts that the settle population is "its own session plus the sessions it observes", but `_population_has_live_work(project, *, session)` filters live pointers to a single session and cannot see `--observe-session` peers.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §4 carries one deliverable (the pane ends when no work is live); the child-settle, host-census-removal and next-dispatch child are all parts of that one goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §4 declares `depends-on` `the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches#s2`, which matches its reliance on the §2 start row for the "new child delivers the next run's start row" bullet, and the declared deps chain (`s4→s2`, `s3→s5`, `s5→s2`) resolves to nodes that exist.
